subject: URGENT: eastus3 performance spike — request to reroute traffic
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, BrightLeaf Ops <ops@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T13:12:00Z
Subject: sudden latency/502s from eastus3

Hi Vanessa —

We started seeing a large spike in 502s and end-to-end latency from our app around 12:45pm ET. Error rate has climbed from ~0.2% to ~9% and p95 latency is up ~3x. This is impacting customers across our northeast region.

We attached an error trace and a short GIF of the spike. Our engineering team is already paged but asked if Redwood has any region-level throttles or routing gone wrong that could explain it. Can you confirm?

Current details:
- Affected region: eastus3 (primary)
- Services: text-generation endpoint (model: rw-instruct-large-v1)
- Impact: 12:45pm — ongoing, ~9% 502s, elevated latencies
- Business impact: customers seeing failed requests in checkout flows

Attachments: error_snapshot.log (txt), traffic_chart_eastus3.png (png)

—Sara Liu
Director of Platform Reliability
BrightLeaf Health

2) If this is capacity saturation, propose an immediate traffic-steer to westus2 or a compatible model variant and estimate cutover time.

I'll keep Sara in loop. If we need SLA credits or prioritized capacity, we'll escalate to leadership.

On Mon, Aug 10, 2027 at 13:12 Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a large spike in 502s and end-to-end latency from our app around 12:45pm ET.

Quick triage notes:
- Observed pattern: request queue growth + transient KV cache thrash on eastus3 serving cluster for rw-instruct-large-v1.
- Node telemetry (13:00-13:40Z): GPU utilization at ~95% on several pods, scheduler latency increased, KV cache miss rate doubled.
- Error manifests as upstream 502s from the runtime (kernel timeouts) rather than user-layer application hits.

Immediate mitigation steps we can take now (est. time-to-effect):
A) Traffic steer to westus2 (compatible instance + same model) — ~6-8 min to shift and validate. Partial steer first (20%) then ramp.
B) Activate burst capacity in eastus3 (if spare) — ~10-12 min but uncertain given current cluster saturation.
C) Enable aggressive prefix/KV cache eviction tuning (risky for QoR) — ~3-5 min to deploy config.

Recommendation: initiate a partial 20% traffic reroute to westus2 now while we increase eastus3 capacity. I'll attach the traffic chart.

Attachments: traffic_chart_eastus3.png

Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi / Jordan — BrightLeaf (DL-78341) is currently seeing revenue impact from eastus3 saturation. Hannah recommends an immediate partial traffic reroute to westus2 (20% then ramp) and spinning up burst capacity in eastus3.

Customer impact: checkout failures for multiple enterprise customers; they have legal/ops teams on standby. If we cannot stabilize in the next 30–45 minutes we should prepare an SLA remediation runbook and CC Legal/Customer Success.

Please:
- Marissa: can you assemble a 15-min exec bridge (15:20Z) and draft a short customer-facing note (2–3 bullet lines) I can send to Sara immediately?
- Rishi: confirm cost/implications of burst capacity and whether we should pre-approve for BrightLeaf (we have an outstanding support request but need faster decision).
- Jordan: please notify Marketplace/Partner ops if there's any potential region-level routing policy we should override.

I'll start the partial steer (20%) at 14:10Z and monitor; will pause if errors increase.

Vanessa Ortiz
